HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Night interior of the Sabi palace colonnade, looking DOWN the long timber hall axis. DUTCH low three-quarter. Foreground, large: Councillor Sunchung mid-stride toward the lens in his vermilion-red court robe and black silk cap with the gold flame ornament, white hair and white beard, a folded memorial clenched in one fist, mouth open remonstrating, not the portrait's clasped-hands stance. Midground, in a side doorway to the right: Councillor Hungsu in his wine-red robe and tall purple cap with the silver flame plaque, half-turned, that small knowing smile, already leaving. Far end of the colonnade, tiny: General Gyebek in ochre-gold and a crimson scarf, steel lamellar, walking out the open doors toward the river, reverse-grip ring-pommel at his hip, back half to us. ONE device: the receding colonnade as a dark timber tunnel. One hanging bronze lamp just outside the left edge of frame rakes across Sunchung's red silk and white beard; gold #c9a24d as the lamp bounce, not a glow. Wine-red #b98f33 catch on Hungsu. Crushed blacks, long shadows climbing the pillars. EXACTLY THREE named people, one of each, never cloned. Ignore any curved sword on Gyebek's portrait. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = seongchung, SECOND face = heungsu, THIRD face = gyebek. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_sabi_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). BOTTOM ROW: the only sword design. SUNCHUNG — Look: Elderly Baekje councillor: long white hair falling past the shoulders from under a small black silk cap with a single gold openwork flame-and-phoenix ornament pinned at the FRONT of the cap; full white beard and white moustache; heavy-lidded tired eyes, a deep crease between the brows, sun-weathered skin. Dress: Deep vermilion-red wide-sleeved court robe over a cream crossed inner collar, a dark indigo-blue sash, two carved jade toggles and a long red tassel hanging at the waist. Colour #c9a24d. HUNGSU — Look: Lean Baekje councillor in late middle age: long silver-grey hair in two falling locks from under a tall dark-purple silk official cap with a silver openwork flame-phoenix plaque on the front and two strings of dark-red beads hanging from the brim with gold tassels; thin grey moustache and a pointed grey chin-beard; half-lidded amused eyes, a small knowing smile. Dress: Deep wine-red / magenta wide-sleeved robe with a gold-brocade crossed collar and heavy gold-brocade cloud-scroll shoulder panels, a dark sash. Colour #b98f33. GYEBEK — Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Colour #d9b13a. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
